shared = {'TAA','TTA','TAG','CTA','TGA','TCA'}

# find runs with no shared stops, allowing any starting offset
def longest_nostop(s):
    best=(0,0)
    n=len(s)
    for start in range(n-2):
        j=start
        while j < n-2:
            if s[j:j+3] in shared:
                break
            j+=3
        run = j-start
        if run > best[1]-best[0]:
            best=(start,j)
    return best

## Report: `region.fasta` (`region_005`, 3,000 bp)

### 1. Basic composition
* Length: 3,000 bp; overall GC 45.4%; sequence contains only A/C/G/T.
* CpG observed/expected ≈ 0.98 → no vertebrate-style CpG island.

### 2. Composition is very heterogeneous in its GC content
A 100-bp sliding window shows the region is not compositionally uniform at all:

| Position (fwd) | GC content |
|---|---|
| 1 – ~520 | **27 – 35 %** (strongly AT‑rich) |
| ~530 – 1,720 | **45 – 62 %**, peaking around nt 870–1,400 (59–62 %) |
| ~1,730 – 2,200 | **34 – 41 %** |
| ~2,300 – 2,500 | ~47 – 52 % |
| ~2,650 – 2,900 | **27 – 40 %** (AT-rich again) |

That is a GC-poor → GC-rich → GC-poor alternation over just 3 kb, with locally extreme values on both ends (28 % GC right next to 62 % GC around nt 1000–1400). This sort of mosaic is the classic signature of **compositionally distinct, horizontally acquired DNA** (e.g. a phage / plasmid / genomic-island fragment) rather than an ordinary stretch of one genome.

### 3. Coding content
Five complete ORFs of ≥90 aa are found; **all of them are on the reverse (crick) strand** (they run right-to-left relative to the FASTA as given). Forward strand contributes nothing above ~50 aa, which is a strong strand asymmetry.

| Coords (fwd strand) | Strand | Length | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 561 – 1350 | − | **263 aa**, ATG…TAA | Sits inside the GC-rich island. Codon usage is markedly GC-biased: Arg 80 % CGN, Thr 54 % ACG, Ala 41 % GCG, Leu 48 % CTG, Ser 47 % AGT — very different from the AT-rich flanks. |
| 1100 – 1358 | − | **86 aa**, ATG…TGA | Nested/overlapping with the 263-aa ORF in a different frame. Unusually Cys+Met-rich (≈ 31 % of residues) and very hydrophobic — could be a small membrane/metal-binding protein, though at this length it may also be spurious. |
| 1424 – 1787 | − | **121 aa**, ATG…TAG | Strikingly basic at the N terminus (…GPEKRRRRTTQEKIAIVQQS…) with a long Ala/Glu-rich tail and no cysteine — composition typical of a small **DNA-binding protein** (partitioning / regulator-type). |
| 2223 – 2619 | − | **132 aa**, ATG…TGA | Composition fairly ordinary; no obvious signal peptide or coiled-coil. |
| 151 – 574 | − | **141 aa**, ATG…TGA | Composition unremarkable (Leu-rich ~13 %). Bounded by the AT-rich left flank. |

### 4. Interpretation
Taken together — one strand of the fragment carries 5 putative CDSs back-to-back, and those CDSs sit in blocks of very different GC content (a 62 % GC island in the middle flanked by ~30 % GC sequence on both sides) — the most parsimonious explanation is that this region is **not ordinary housekeeping chromosomal DNA, but a fragment of a mobile genetic element** (prophage, plasmid, or genomic island) that was integrated into an AT-rich host genome (or vice versa). The internal GC contrast further suggests the fragment itself may be a **fusion of two horizontally acquired segments**, with the compact GC-rich coding island around nt 560–1720 being the most obvious programme-level feature.

### 5. What I did *not* do
I analysed sequence composition, codon usage, and ORFs only — I did **not** run a BLAST/protein-domain search, look for direct/inverted repeats, terminators, ribosome-binding sites, or RNA features, so functional assignments above (e.g. the 121-aa basic protein as a DNA-binding protein) are compositional inferences, not homology-based identifications. A BLASTP search of the three larger ORFs against the nr database would be the natural next step.
